findings.location: source_order musaf_adir_first / musaf_tisgav_custom / musaf_veyeetayu_custom (lines ~6110-6219); expanded_order same sections (lines ~11610, ~11786, ~11898)
findings.problem: The new conditions use the opensiddur:rite feature `frankfurt`. The project already has a Frankfurt condition: torah_berikh_shema_custom (line ~5518) uses `frankfurt_am_main`. A volume or setting that declares frankfurt_am_main=true will not remove the first Adir, Tisgav or Veyeetayu. Each of those conditions evaluates to undefined, so the texts the edition says Frankfurt omits are printed for Frankfurt.
findings.required_fix: Use one Frankfurt rite feature across the whole project. Either rename the new `frankfurt` to the existing `frankfurt_am_main`, or migrate the old feature deliberately. Apply the change in both spines. Then re-check the truth tables: frankfurt=true must make first Adir, Tisgav and Veyeetayu false.

findings.location: musaf_tisgav_custom features.marmorstein_tisgav; musaf_veyeetayu_custom any(...marmorstein_veyeetayu) in both spines
findings.problem: Each unresolved opt-in custom ('many congregations do not say it') is modelled as an opensiddur:rite feature named after this edition. JLPTEI says a wording that some communities add and others omit is an opensiddur:variant whose feature name is a condition URN, and that this variant belongs to the text, not to the edition. The project already follows that rule for the same pattern: rite frankfurt_am_main=false plus variant urn:x-opensiddur:condition:prayer:berikh_shemeh/torah_opening=true (lines ~5514-5526). The marmorstein_* names would add edition-specific pseudo-rites to the settings, and no other source could reuse them.
findings.required_fix: Replace marmorstein_tisgav and marmorstein_veyeetayu with opensiddur:variant condition URNs that mirror the text, e.g. urn:x-opensiddur:condition:prayer:amidah/tisgav_levaddekha/<name> and urn:x-opensiddur:condition:poem:v_yeetayu_kol_leavdekha/<name>. Name them by the transliteration rules and register them. Keep the rite parts (Frankfurt/Metz false, Fuerth true) and leave the variants undefined by default.

findings.problem: The documentary witness itself uses the Bible URN urn:x-opensiddur:text:bible:numbers/15/41/b as its root URN, in both HE and EN, and it carries the speaker קו״ח inside that scope. The expanded order transcludes numbers/15/41/b and also adds its own קו״ח rubric, so the actor prints twice. This also differs from how the parallel Shema is handled: musaf_qedushah_shema uses a siddur quote-context URN, and the expanded order reuses the morning owner of deuteronomy/6/4. No registry search or morning-owner comparison was supplied for 15:41b. Numbers 15:41 is already owned by the morning shacharit_numbers_15_37_to_41. If that HE owner carries half-verse milestones, /b is now claimed twice and the first claim (the morning wording) wins. The EN unit also claims a half-verse, which a translation normally cannot carry.
findings.required_fix: Encode the witness like the Shema witness: a siddur:rosh_hashanah/musaf/repetition/qedushah/... context URN with quote-context chapter/verse milestones and source=bible:numbers/15/41 (part b), and no Bible URN on the root. In the expanded order, reference numbers/15/41/b only if exactly one owner per project resolves to the s246/s247 wording. Otherwise reference a canonical owner that has no speaker. Make sure the actor rubric appears exactly once.

findings.problem: The reference runs from target prayer:amidah/vetimlokh_attah_hashem/vetimlokh to targetEnd bible:psalms/146/10. A JLPTEI range cannot cross namespace/work: the end form keeps the start's namespace-and-work component. So this cannot be serialised as one j:transclude range. By contrast, qadosh_attah → qedushat_hashem/hamelekh_haqadosh stays inside prayer:amidah and can be expressed with the absolute form.
findings.required_fix: Replace it with a reference that can be serialised. Either target the vetimlokh_attah_hashem root, if its resolved extent is exactly the vetimlokh part plus the verse, or use one transclusion. In either case confirm that the vetimlokh prayer-part scope, which a verse milestone does not end, does not already include the verse, so the verse cannot appear twice. Verify the compiled HE/EN extent, including the plene_sheva / shall_reign declarations.

findings.location: unit musaf_qedushah_adir HE/EN psalms/8/10 blocks (lines 3947-3959, 3990-4002); parts addir (3936, 3979), echad_hu (3741, 3770), tisgav (4143, 4173)
findings.problem: (a) Inside the new canonical Adir, Psalm 8:10 uses the real Bible URN bible:psalms/8/10 as its corresp, but its chapter_corresp is a quote context (addir_adiraynu/quotations/psalms_8). It also has no reference_unit and no end_reference. Zechariah 14:9 in the same prayer is quote-context only. That makes the canonical prayer claim a full Bible verse, which the user's rule and JLPTEI quote-context guidance forbid for quoted verses. Mixing a canonical verse milestone with a contextual chapter milestone is also inconsistent. (b) The named parts echad_hu, addir and tisgav have no reference_unit, while the Kesod parts use prayer-part. Without milestone units the part scope is undefined. With prayer-part and no later prayer-part milestone, `addir` would cover the whole prayer instead of just אַדִּיר אַדִּירֵנוּ.
findings.required_fix: Make Psalm 8:10 quote-context: corresp addir_adiraynu/quotations/psalms_8/10 with reference_unit verse and source=bible:psalms/8/10, closed before the next quotation. Give echad_hu, addir and tisgav an explicit unit (prayer-part) and terminators, so each part covers only its own words. Re-verify that the repeat ranges echad_hu→quotations/numbers_15/41 and addir→quotations/zechariah_14/9 resolve to exactly the printed text.

findings.location: wording_variants musaf_qedushah_mimeqomo_en_15, musaf_qedushah_echad_hu_he_16 / _en_17 (lines 14383-14433); wording_selection in musaf_qedushah_mimeqomo_repeat and musaf_qedushah_echad_hu_repeat; expanded declarations
findings.problem: These condition URNs are named …/first_printing and …/second_printing. The names describe this edition's print order, not the wording. JLPTEI requires variant URNs that belong to the text, and the project's other variants are descriptive (haaretz_with_meteg, kol_with_maqaf_shiltan, for_ever/forever). In echad_hu one feature pair controls both a Hebrew vowel (כָּל־חָי / כָּל־חַי) and English punctuation (‘father. He is our King,’ / ‘father, He is our king,’…). A setting therefore cannot choose one without the other, and no other edition can reuse the names.
findings.required_fix: Rename them with descriptive wording names, separately per language where the differences are independent, e.g. echad_hu/chai_qamatz vs chai_patach for HE, and a punctuation-named pair for EN; likewise mimeqomo/proclaim vs proclaims. Update the wording_variants entries, the unit wording_selection and the expanded declarations together.

notes: I checked both spines against source-blocks.json. Documentary and expanded order match the printed sequence exactly: Kesod → Qadosh → Kevodo(ק׳) → Vechayyot → Kevodo(ח׳) → Barukh(קו״ח) → Mimeqomo(ק׳) → Veammekha → Mimeqomo(ח׳) → Shema(קו״ח) → Echad(ק׳) → Veattah → Echad(ח׳) → Ani(קו״ח) → [Frankfurt rubric] Adir(ק׳) → Tehillot → Adir(ק׳) → Uvedivrei(ח׳) → Yimlokh(קו״ח) → Ledor(ח׳) → Ki Maqdishekha/Od Yizkar → open Ark → Haochez → close Ark → [rubric] Tisgav(ח״) → three Uvekhen → [Fuerth rubric] Veyeetayu → Vetimlokh → Qadosh Attah/HaMelekh HaQadosh. Apart from the Ani duplicate, the actor rubrics match the print.

Every variant declaration matches its witness: qadosh haaretz_with_meteg (s238); barukh_kevod without maqaf (s240); mimeqomo defective/plene (s240/s242), with human readings 364/367 present in both; ledor_vador dor_defective (s246); Yimlokh abbreviated+sheva / will_reign_in_eternity (s246/s247); Vetimlokh plene+sheva / shall_reign (s252/s253); pachdekha with maqaf + shiltan (s250); kavod land_without_comma (s251). The 5 formulas and 4 Qedushah parts reuse the existing identities.

These identity decisions are correctly applied: Kesod starts at כְּסוֹד with no Naaritzekha words added; Kevodo/Mimeqomo; legacy addir_adiraynu; Veyeetayu reuses the existing root and /1–8 (the stanza-3 milestone stays outside the optional clause); the Echad canonical claims only a quote-context for Numbers 15:41; Zechariah 14:9 at Adir and Tisgav is quote-context only; the first Adir alone carries the Frankfurt condition and the repeat is unconditional.

Tisgav logic is correct: omitted for Frankfurt or Metz, otherwise undefined and kept with its rubric. Veyeetayu is correctly false for Frankfurt or Metz. Note that fuerth=true alone gives undefined (text kept with its description), not true; it becomes true only when Frankfurt and Metz are also false. That follows from the declared truth tables and is acceptable, but should be documented.

The rubric types are right: the Adir and Tisgav German/Hebrew rubrics are condition instructions, the Fuerth rubric is a description because it says who sings what, the Ark open/close lines are directives, and the ק׳/ח׳/קו״ח/ח״ marks are descriptions. סאַלטעט and the corrected פֿראַנקפֿורט/מעץ are kept unnormalised, and the English rubric is kept as printed even though it leaves out Metz.

Page flags were set only on the new witnesses, and all of them match page-decisions.json. The new documentary instructions are correctly page_start=false. The s252 displacement is implemented as described (deferred_page_boundary on the first unconditional continuation, raw scan kept on the fragment).

Untranslated content stays empty: Vechayyot has English only for Rachem; the Frankfurt Adir rubric and the Ark and acrostic rubrics are Hebrew only. Source notes record this, and no English was supplied.
Corrections: musaf_harachum_shehu and musaf_kesod_once_one are installed. rh_pachdekha_hast is content-bound with attestations s27/s251, and the s119/s203 corrections stay local, as specified.
